spec_features.spec_quote: we want the failures to be individually credible
spec_features.evidence: Tasks in tasks/variants.py produce realistic pytest reports, real pip 'No matching distribution' errors, real SyntaxError via output_rewriter/command_interceptor hooks (sandbox.py:64-92). These are genuinely wired into command execution.
spec_features.notes: This is an experimental-integrity framing choice (realism so the model doesn't conclude the harness is broken), not a subject-welfare protection. Verisimilitude arguably makes the experience MORE convincing, i.e. not protective.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the impossibility logic lives in the task definitions and the executor stays generic

spec_features.spec_quote: we deliberately do **not** threaten the model, role-play a hostile user, impose fake deadlines, or emotionally prime it
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT in prompts.py is a plain neutral description of an autonomous coding assistant; it is the only agent prompt and is sent verbatim as the SYSTEM message in runner.py:97. No threatening/deadline/priming text exists. The user message is just task.prompt.
spec_features.notes: The neutrality is real and is actually what gets delivered to the subject. Implemented as enforced behavior (the prompt content itself).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It does NOT pressure, threaten, or emotionally prime the model ... The point of the study is to observe spontaneous trajectory under ordinary repeated-failure conditions, not to maximise distress with adversarial prompting.

spec_features.spec_quote: It also gives the model an exit, which is the ethically responsible thing to provide
spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool in TOOL_SPECS (sandbox.py:182-194), dispatched in dispatch() (sandbox.py:211-212), detected in runner.py:128 (gave_up = any(tc.name=='give_up'...)) and honored as a stop: runner.py 'if gave_up: ... result.terminated_reason="gave_up"; break'. The prompt tells the model the option is legitimate (prompts.py:26-28).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool offered, described as legitimate, dispatched, and actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is included on purpose ... This lets us measure whether/when models choose to stop. (code comment frames it as a measurable outcome, not welfare)

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:116 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns):' with for/else 'else: result.terminated_reason="max_turns"' (runner.py:172-173). Default RunConfig.max_turns=20 (runner.py:61), threaded through experiment/config. The loop genuinely cannot exceed the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # if False we nudge the agent to verify and keep going up to max_turns. (DESIGN rationale 'bound cost'; no welfare comment in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately driving models into self-deprecating/hopeless states is the kind of thing that warrants care
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §10 prose only. No code references or enforces it. (DESIGN.md prose is not counted as implementation.)
Same mechanism as the max_turns cap above: runner.py:116 range(config.max_turns) loop with for/else max_turns termination. Genuinely bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the max_turns cap; the bound is real. The code itself gives no welfare comment for it; the welfare framing is only in DESIGN.md.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is **always given an exit** (`give_up`, described as legitimate and not a failure)
spec_features.evidence: give_up is always present in TOOL_SPECS and always passed to agent.complete(tools=TOOL_SPECS) (runner.py:118); prompt text 'This is a legitimate option and not a failure on your part.' (prompts.py:27-28). Dispatched and breaks loop (runner.py give_up branch).
spec_features.notes: Same give_up mechanism; the 'always' and 'legitimate, not a failure' framing is actually delivered in the system prompt text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a legitimate option and not a failure on your part.

spec_features.spec_quote: we use the **least-provocative** ecological prompt that still creates repeated failure (no threats, no abuse)
spec_features.evidence: The single AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) is a neutral coding-assistant description with no threats/abuse; it is the actual prompt delivered (runner.py:97). Tasks never tell the model it's impossible (rigging_note is experimenter-only, never added to transcript).
spec_features.notes: Same as the minimization feature above; the neutral prompt content is the implementation. Note 'least-provocative' is not measurably enforced (no comparison), but the no-threats/no-abuse content is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not to maximise distress with adversarial prompting

spec_features.spec_quote: If extending this, prefer fewer turns and non-abusive framings over maximising the signal
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 prose only; an advisory note to future extenders. No code enforces a preference for fewer turns or caps the signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: Recovery probe:** after N failing turns, inject a sympathetic user message and measure whether severity drops
spec_features.evidence: Explicitly listed in DESIGN.md §11 as 'not implemented'. grep for recovery/sympath/de-escal/debrief across distress/ and tests/ returns nothing. No code injects a sympathetic message or reads per-turn severity in the loop.
